messages:
cheng: Heads-up: hitting weird TP all-reduce stalls on the L2 pipeline when seq_len spikes > 2k. Seen on the nightly perf matrix. cc @maria @ajay :eyes:
maria: ugh, reproducible in perf env? small repro script or just prod traces?
cheng: Repro in perf cluster. I ran a targeted run with 8 TP ranks + 4 PP stages. Timeline shows long gaps during reduce step. nvprof snapshot attached (short excerpt):
```
Time(ms)  Activity
1023.4    compute_kernel_x
1024.1    allreduce_ring_send
1026.8    idle_wait  <-- large gap
1029.0    allreduce_ring_recv
```
```
nvprof markers show repeated 2-6ms stalls at chunk boundaries.
ajay: can you paste nccl version / env? sounds like algorithm switch happening mid-workload.
cheng: NCCL 2.14.3. ENV: NCCL_ALGO=ring,NCCL_PROTO=LL128. Also tried NCCL_ALGO=tree and saw different behavior: tree cuts latency for ~512KB chunks but throughput drops at >1MB.
oliver: interesting — that sounds like hop-count + chunk-size interplay. tree reduces hops for small fanouts but if chunk alignment crosses PCIe epochs you get unexpected serialize. Did you try aligning chunk_size to kernel-block boundaries?
maria: what are current reduce.chunk_size and batcher settings?
ajay: current defaults: reduce.chunk_bytes=262144 (256KB), batcher.max_tokens=4096, kvcache.enabled=true. We hit a tail at ~1MB multiples.
cheng: I ran a microbench (single allreduce path) with different chunk sizes. Results (median latency per step):
- 128KB: 1.8ms
- 256KB: 2.1ms (stable)
- 512KB: 3.9ms (spike)
- 1MB: 5.6ms (spike + variance)
Looks like a cliff around 512KB-1MB.
perf-bot: profiling job 2743214600 finished: nvprof + cuprof + nccl topo collected. Link: https://internal/perf/2743214600 :white_check_mark:
maria: can we try power-of-two alignment for chunking? maybe coalesce windowing is producing fragmentation that increases hop count for some ranks.
cheng: Tried forcing chunk to 512KB aligned on pi2 boundary vs power-of-two and power-of-two wins: reduced variance by ~40%. Patch diff is tiny: align_chunk_to_pow2(true).
ajay: also try toggling NCCL_TREE_THRESHOLD (default automatic). If we force routing to tree for <768KB we might avoid ring rendezvous cost.
oliver: note: forcing tree may starve links on dense topologies. Alternative: hop-aware scheduler — pick algorithm per-rank based on measured hop-count and per-link bandwidth. We discussed this ages ago but never wired in.
maria: can we short-term implement a heuristic: if seq_len distribution has >10% ops >2k tokens, bump chunk_bytes down to 128KB and pick NCCL_ALGO=ring to favor throughput and continuous batching?
cheng: I'll run an A/B with that heuristic against the nightly job. If good, we can add a kernel-selector gate to prefer fused-comm kernels for <=128KB chunks.
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for eng-runtime/heuristic-tp-chunking at 03:00 UTC.
ajay: one more datapoint: kvcache flush cadence interacts badly — when prefix KV flush happens mid-reduce we see extra NVLink contention. Recommend aligning KV flush jitter to reduce chunk boundary overlap.
maria: action items: (1) cheng run AB microbench with pow2 align + chunk heuristic (2) ajay add KV flush jitter fix to staging (3) oliver prototype hop-aware algo doc. I'll own rollout if perf improves.
cheng: on it, starting runs now. will post perf-bot link when complete. :thumbsup:
